opens.note: The offering that rises whole in smoke; the name comes from ʿalah, “go up.”

payoffs.note: The going up offering is already burning on the altar when the fat is laid on it.

threads.note: The offering the book keeps returning to: ordinary, ordination, eighth day, Day of Coverings.

opens.note: The verb of the whole approach: the offerer brings the animal near, and the priests bring the blood near.

payoffs.note: The verb is the frame of the chapter: the offerer brings near the animal, then from it brings near the fire offering (3:1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 12, 14).

threads.note: The book's verb of access; it names the qorban, the brought near offering.

opens.note: First use here, with the going up offering; the rendering is cover, with purge or expiate in the note.

threads.note: The book's central act, from the first chapter to the Day of Coverings.

opens.note: The offering's refrain; niḥoaḥ ties it to Noaḥ's offering and the root of rest.

payoffs.note: The refrain of 1:9, now said of the fat pieces.

threads.note: A fixed refrain with a Genesis root.

opens.note: The name for what goes up in fire; the sense food gift is in the note.

payoffs.note: What reaches the altar here is only the fat pieces, not the whole animal as in chapter 1.

threads.note: The book's standard word for what reaches the altar.

opens.note: The offerer leans a hand on the animal's head: here one hand, later two on the goat sent away.

payoffs.note: The same act as the going up offering (1:4), now on an animal of either sex; repeated for the sheep (3:8) and the goat (3:13).

threads.note: Returns at the blasphemer in the book's last narrative.

opens.note: Kept apart from saraf, “burn”: the altar's act is to turn the offering into smoke.

payoffs.note: The priests' verb for the fat pieces (3:5, 11, 16), as for the whole going up offering in 1:9.

threads.note: A distinct altar verb across the offering and priestly narratives.

opens.note: minḥah, the book's own word for the grain gift: fine flour with oil and frankincense (2:1). Elsewhere the word is wider, any gift, as Gen 4:3.

threads.note: Rendered "gift offering" so that the wider sense of a gift stays in view; Lev 2 says what this one is made of.

opens.note: ʾazkarah, from zakhar "remember": the handful the priest turns into smoke from the gift offering (2:2, 9, 16). Why it is called this is argued.

threads.note: A rare word tied to the handful: Lev 2:2, 9, 16; Num 5:26; Lev 6:15; 24:7.

opens.note: ḥeleb, the fat that covers and lies on the innards and kidneys, the part that belongs to Yahweh (3:3–4, 9–10, 14–17). The law that closes the chapter, no fat and no blood, is stated again in 7:23–25 and 17:6.

threads.note: Rendered "fat", the plain word; the notes say it is the fat that can be peeled off, not the fat running through the meat.

opens.note: shelamim, the offering of the animal from herd, flock or goats whose meat the offerer eats (3:1, 3, 6, 9). Nobody knows quite where the word comes from; the English name is a choice.

threads.note: Rendered "well-being offering", from shalom; chapter 3 does not say who eats, 7:11–36 does.
